title: The 2024 SYSK Christmas Extravaganza!
summary: Holiday special episode of Stuff You Should Know covering a range of Christmas topics: Holly Iten Miller's "Grandma's Christmas Breath" cocktail (tasted on air), the White Elephant gift game (Dirty Santa) and its rules and origin, pizzelle cookies, bûche de Noël, White House Christmas trees and record counts, the first Christmas movie (Santa Claus, 1898), and the 1982 animated special Ziggy's Gift. Includes a short sponsor-free intro and sign-off with holiday wishes.
topics: White Elephant origin Siam albino elephant

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts open the Christmas episode, note it is ad-free and the last recording of the year, and preview the holiday theme.

segments.title: Grandma's Christmas Breath cocktail
segments.summary: Chuck mixes a holiday cocktail submitted by listener Holly Iten Miller, Grandma's Christmas Breath, using gingerbread rum, Grand Marnier, and orange juice, and gives his tasting impressions.

segments.title: White Elephant gift game
segments.summary: The hosts explain the White Elephant (Dirty Santa) gift exchange: the name's origin from a king of Siam giving albino elephants, typical rules such as a dollar limit, the stealing mechanics, three-steal limits, and ending the game. They also discuss punch variations.

segments.title: Pizzelle and bûche de Noël
segments.summary: The hosts cover pizzelle, an Italian waffle-iron cookie known as a Christmas and Easter treat, suggested by listener Carl Hardin, and then the French bûche de Noël, its origins as a yule log tradition, and the 1890 recipe attributed to Pierre Lacome.

segments.title: White House Christmas trees
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the first White House Christmas tree in 1889, electric lights, Teddy Roosevelt and the tree, Eisenhower's record of 26 trees, later record counts, Blue Room tree competition, and the tree species and states with the most selections.

segments.title: First Christmas movie
segments.summary: The hosts trace early film history from the Lumière brothers and Louis Le Prince to George Albert Smith's 1898 film Santa Claus, which is considered the first Christmas movie, and describe its special effects.

segments.title: Ziggy's Gift animated special
segments.summary: The hosts praise the 1982 Ziggy's Gift TV special, its animation effort, Emmy win over competitors, its silent-character casting choice, and its fading from TV listings after 1986.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wish listeners a merry Christmas and happy holidays, mention the crew, and close the episode.
